observations: The page number «64» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01-L17 end chapter 17, after the example of the latitude of Venus begun on p. 63 (JP2 0095, L32-L41). L18-L19 and L34-L35: the headings of chapters 18 and 19, in bold, centred, each with the reference to the text below it.

L01 and L08: the colons of the divisions are set with a word space on either side (26-32 px measured), written ∶ (U+2236); «1p», the p raised and italic. L07-L08: «also ist die Breite =» at the left, and the formula «54,5′ ∶ 1,25 = c. 44′.» displayed, centred, its base line about 25 px below that of L07.

L01-L08. Checked: 3° 54′ = 234′, and 234′ : 1.25 = 187.2′, 187′ = 3° 7′; leaving out the anomaly, 59° 27′ + 131° 1′ = 190° 28′ (p. 63, JP2 0095, L37-L40); 54½′ : 1.25 = 43.6′, about 44′. The values of Table 50 are to be compared with the table.
L16-L17: the fractions «9/8» and «grösste Breite / r′» printed built up within the line, written {fr:NUMERATOR|DENOMINATOR}.

L24-L33. Checked: the hourly motion of the moon's apogee, 16″ 42‴ 27⁗, times twenty-four is 6′ 40″ 58‴ 48⁗ (as on p. 15, JP2 0047), so that the daily motion of the text, 6′ 40″ 18‴ (chapter 18, p. 15, JP2 0047, L04), should be 6′ 40″ 58‴, as Suter says; in the abjad 18 is yāʾ ḥāʾ and 58 nūn ḥāʾ, letters distinguished by their dots. 360° in 3231.466 days are 6′ 41.1″ a day; 3231.466 days are 8.85 Julian years, «c. 9a».
L26: «27IV», the fourths written with a raised italic IV; L28: «3231,466d», the d raised; L29: «9a», the a raised. L09: «Batt.’s» in italics and not spaced, where it is spaced elsewhere on the page.

L36-L38. Checked against chapter 19 of the Latin text (p. 15, JP2 0047, L08-L12): Saturn three signs 13° 12′, Jupiter two signs 22° 1′, Mars 21° 54′, Venus one sign 29° 27′, Mercury 21° 10′, that is 103° 12′, 82° 1′, 21° 54′, 59° 27′ and 21° 10′; «(44′)» for Mars is the reading XLIIII of C and M (p. 15, note 12). These are the values that the text adds to the place of the planet for the argument of latitude (chapter 17, p. 14, JP2 0046, L10-L11), as in the example of Saturn on p. 62 (JP2 0094, L36). The values are set in five columns, the names over them; each printed row is one line here, the cells separated by our «|». L38: «21° 10.» without the prime after 10; see the critical note.

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Batt.», «Kh.», «Thibaut»; italics: «Breite» (L01, L07), «Venus», «Anomalia aequata», «nördlich.», «Sūrya-Siddhānta», «Panchasiddhāntikā», «r′», «sublimatio», «sullimatio», «submissio»; «lat. sec.» and «lat.» (L06) upright.
The other colons and the semicolons stand after the thin space of the edition (9-15 px measured).

critical_notes.evidence: the other longitudes of the list have the sign of the minutes, «103° 12′», «82° 1′», and the Latin gives «dakaicae X» (p. 15, JP2 0047, L12); the prime after 10 is not printed
